title: Capacity in Litres and Millilitres
introduction: Build on Primary 1 knowledge and practise capacity in litres and millilitres.
definition: Liquid volume is measured in litres (L) and millilitres (mL). Read the scale on a measuring jug at eye level and estimate by comparing with a known container. Capacity is the maximum volume a container can hold.

visuals.label: 1 L = 1,000 mL
visuals.description: A litre can be divided into two 500 mL parts.
visuals.alt: 1 L = 1,000 mL — A litre can be divided into two 500 mL parts.

examples.question: A measuring jug shows 400 mL.
steps: Read the level against its marked scale.

examples.question: A bottle holds about twice the volume of a 250 mL cup.

exercises.question: A jug shows 600 mL. Volume in mL?
Which unit suits a large bucket: mL or L?
A container holds about four 250 mL cups. Estimate mL.
How many millilitres make one litre?
Which holds more: 200 mL or 750 mL? Enter mL.
A bottle is marked 2 L. Capacity in litres?

summary: Liquid volume is measured in litres (L) and millilitres (mL). Read the scale on a measuring jug at eye level and estimate by comparing with a known container. Capacity is the maximum volume a container can hold.
